question.leadin: Answer the following about ancient rulers who name cylinders.
question.text: What is believed to be the world's first declaration of human rights was inscribed on this ruler's namesake cylinder. This "Great" ruler of the Persian Empire freed the Jews from the Babylonian Captivity.
question.clue: This son of Persis seized the city of Sardis after defeating the Lydian king, Croesus.

swap.leadin: This man born as Codomannus took the throne following the scheming of the Vizier Bagoas.
swap.text: Name this final ruler of the Persian Achaemenid Empire who lost the battles of Issus and Gaugamela.
swap.clue: This monarch was served by Memnon of Rhodes, and this man's Cardaces were completely destroyed at a engagement in which his wife Stateria I was captured, that was the Battle of Issus.

question.leadin: Though Susa was the official capital of this empire, Persepolis was the ceremonial capital.
question.text: Name this empire founded by Cyrus the Great in modern-day Iran. Kings named Darius and Xerxes led this empire.
question.clue: That same ruler became a(+) messiah after returning the Israelites to their homeland, which ended the Babylonian Captivity.

swap.leadin: This battle followed Alexander the Great's victory at the Granicus River.
swap.text: Name this first of two major victories for Alexander the Great over Darius III, which took place in 333 BCE. Darius fled inward after this battle, allowing Alexander to consolidate his conquests.
swap.clue: In addition to that defeat of Pescennius Niger, this was the site of a 1266 battle at which King Hethum I of Armenia was defeated by Baibars.

question.leadin: Answer the following about conflicts within the Byzantine Empire.
question.text: The Byzantine Empire nearly ended during an early 7th century war with this empire, at the time led by Khosrow II. This empire was based in the same region as the earlier Achaemenid Empire.
question.answerHtml: Sasanian Empire [or Neo-Persian Empire or Empire of the Iranians; accept “Sassanid” in place of Sasanian]
question.clue: The main feature remaining from this empire's capital is the Taq Kasra brickwork vault.

swap.leadin: A ruler of this empire captured Valerian at the Battle of Edessa and used him as a footstool.
swap.text: Name this Zoroastrian empire which displaced the Parthian Empire in the 3rd Century CE. Ardashir andShapur the Great were rulers of this empire based in Ctesiphon.

question.text: This Elamite city served as the capital of Cyrus the Great before Xerxes' father Darius I built a new one at Persepolis.
question.clue: A polity that called itself Haltamti transferred its capital from Anshan to this city, and this "great holy city" suffered a brutal sack by Ashurbanipal.

swap.leadin: The Achaeminid or Persian Empire was established by Cyrus the Great in the sixth century BCE after he overthrew the Median Empire.
swap.text: Darius the Great created 20 provinces in the Persian Empire. Each province had one of these people that were appointed by Darius himself.
swap.clue: 26 positions with this title were established around 580 BCE, a number that later increased to 36 according to the Behistun Inscription.

question.text: The Ten Thousand were originally hired to fight for Cyrus the Younger against his brother Artaxerxes II. Cyrus the Younger died in this battle when his forces were betrayed by Tissaphernes.
question.clue: Clearchus took command of one side's army after this battle, but was himself later murdered at a banquet given by Tissaphernes.

swap.text: The Sassanids proselytized this state religion of theirs, though it did not spread as far as Manichaeism or Christianity. This religion venerates Ahura Mazda.
swap.answerHtml: Zoroastrianism [accept Mazdayasna or Mazdaism; do not accept or prompt on "Mazdakism"]
swap.clue: This religion whose followers began converting to Islam after the fall of the Sassanids and Arab conquest of Persia.

question.leadin: The third and fourth kings of this name were separated from their rule by Pharnaces I.
question.text: Give this name for six kings of Pontus, the last of whom massacred 80,000 Romans in Anatolia and prompted Sulla, Murena, and Lucullus to fight three namesake wars against him.
question.answerHtml: Mithridates [or Mithridates the Great; or Eupator Dionysius from any confused folks]
question.clue: After conquering the territory of Nicomedes IV of Bithynia, a king of this name massacred all of its Roman citizens in the "Asiatic Vespers".

swap.text: By dethroning his grandfather Astyages, Cyrus ended this empire, which was led from Ecbatana. Under Cyaxares, this empire took part in the conquest of Neo-Assyria.
swap.clue: As a result of a battle at the Halys River, that waterway was declared its border with Lydia.

question.text: The Parthian ruling dynasty was named after this founding ruler, who ruled from the city of Nisa after he conquered a satrapy from the anti-Seleucid rebel Andragoras.

swap.text: The "House of Wisdom" was based on the Academy of Gondishapur, the intellectual center of this dynasty. This dynasty sent the physician Borzuya to India to translate the Panchatantra.
swap.clue: One king of this dynasty was crowned in utero, while another may have either flayed the skin of a noted captive or poured molten gold down his throat after forcing him and his army to work on an aqueduct, the Band-e-Kaisar.

question.text: This Sassanid city was the site of an A.D. 363 battle that took place between Shapur II and Emperor Julian, which saw a tactical victory for the Romans. It was the primary capital for both the Parthian and Sassanid Empires.
question.clue: This city was known by Arabs as "al- Mada'in" or "the cities" due to its many suburbs, one of which was sarcastically dubbed "better than Antioch," while another was home to the patriarch of the Nestorian church.

swap.text: The Battle of al-Qadisayyah forced this last Sassanian emperor to flee; he was killed by a miller in 651, ending the Sassanian dynasty.

question.leadin: This man made an alliance with Nabopolassar, which resulted in the destruction of Nineveh and the Neo-Assyrian Empire.
question.text: Name this third and greatest king of the Medes, according to Herodotus. At the very end of his long reign, he fought the Battle of Halys River against Lydia, which infamously ended with an eclipse. After that, he was succeeded by the final Median king, Astyages.

swap.text: Later in his reign, Sargon defeated and exiled this ruler who founded Ecbatana and, per Herodotus, was the first king of the Medes.

question.text: Valerian lost at Edessa to the first Sassanid ruler of this name, the son of founder Ardeshir I, who prompted Gordian's murder by Philip the Arab after winning the Battle of Misiche but saw his harem raided by Balista. The second ruler of this name fought Pap and Arshak II of Armenia and killed Julian the Apostate outside Ctesiphon.
question.clue: A king with this name built a namesake city on the road between Estakhr and Ctesiphon.

swap.leadin: Name these people or battles important in Cyrus' establishment of the Persian Empire, FTP each.
swap.text: Cyrus began his conquest by overthrowing this Median king, the son of Cyaxares, and, according to Herodotus, Cyrus' grandfather.
swap.clue: The son of Cyaxares and grandfather of Cyrus the Great, he ruled as the last king of the Medes until Cyrus overthrew him.
